title.narrative: Community led Ecosystem Restoration in Farm-Forest Landscapes in Sierra Leone and Liberia

description.narrative: (1) To enhance environmental protection and sustainable natural resource management through evidence-based strategies, innovative tools, effective capacity building and improved forest governance. (2) Reverse environmental degradation through locally led forest restoration and ecosystem conservation approaches.(3) Improve livelihoods and climate resilience for vulnerable rural communities by strengthening ecosystem-based business and promoting climate-smart agricultural practices.

In Liberia, the program targets 30 communities across 4 clans, in Suakoko district in Bong County that have lost forest and tree cover or are situated at the fringes of forests, where human activities threaten the forest’s sustainability. Bong county, with Suakoko as its largest commercial hub, recorded Liberia’s highest tree cover loss, totaling 409 kha between 2001 and 2023 . With an estimated population of 44,930 across three clans, Suakoko is a critical area for reforestation. To address urgent reforestation needs and prevent further deforestation, the program aims to reach 7,500 farming households, to conserve 50ha per community and to restore 150 hectares of degraded and forest-edge land. Engaging multiple communities and targeting both state and nonstate actors, marginalised groups, and 50% women, ensures that ecosystems benefit and sustainable livelihood opportunities reach those who traditionally have had limited access, thereby promoting fairness, social equity and sustainability.

The aim is to restore degraded forests, preserve biodiversity, protect livelihoods, and combat climate change, through an integrated, sustainable, and resilient approach. The program will start with locally led participatory research to identify priority areas and threats to biodiversity. Using satellite-based land cover analysis, ecosystem dynamics and their impacts on local communities will be better understood. This data will inform the development of a user-friendly mobile application for data collection and monitoring, and the implementation of community led conservation and restoration plans.
